To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatio-temporal organization of carbon and oxygen isotopic signals in Mediterranean oak trees is strongly dependent on the functional type (deciduous vs. evergreen) and that the climate sensitivity of these isotopic signals varies between the functional groups.
Mediterranean deciduous oak trees are more sensitive to drought, while evergreen trees are more sensitive than the former to temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new statistical tools to analyse tree-ring isotope data, which can be used to identify functional groups of trees that are ecologically relevant and to assess their differential responses to environmental drivers across space and time.
the spatio-temporal structure of carbon and oxygen isotopic signals and its implications for understanding the ecological responses of Mediterranean oaks to climate change.

the identification of the most appropriate scale to investigate climate-tree-ring relationships, and provides a useful framework for the study of climate sensitivity in other tree species and ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spatiotemporally structured variability of stable isotopes in oak tree rings provides a valuable source of information to unravel the functional traits that are associated with the ecological strategies of Mediterranean oaks.
the spatial organization of isotopic signals is more important in Mediterranean evergreen oaks than in deciduous species, while the opposite is true for the temporal organization of signals.

the spatiotemoral organization of isotopic signals in Mediterranean oakes is strongly dependent on functional group and, to a lesser extent, on geographical location, which is consistent with the idea that the functional traits of Mediterranean oaks are more important than geographical location in determining their response to environmental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for Mediterranean oaks, the temporal and spatial signals of carbon and oxygen stable isotopes are structured according to the functional group to which the species belong, and the spatial signals are more sensitive to climate than the temporal ones.
Mediterranean oaks are a heterogeneous functional group in terms of water-use efficiency and carbon isotope discrimination.
, in Mediterranean oaks, climate sensitivity is mainly driven by functional group identity, while the spatial organization of tree-ring isotopic signals is mainly determined by the species identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatiotemporally structured signals of tree-ring isotopes are not only a source of noise, but also provide valuable insights into the physiological responses of trees to climate.
, when analysing tree-ring isotopic data, it is essential to consider both spatial and temporal variability to identify the underlying mechanisms of tree growth.

the spatiotemporality of signal strength in tree rings can be used to identify and characterize functional groups, and thus provide a new tool to assess the ecological and physiological implications of tree-ring signals.
